title: Borsuk-Ulam Dimension Formula for Composite n
description: The central open question from equivariant Borsuk-Ulam theory: for composite n ≥ 2, is buDim(n, d) = max_{p|n, p prime} buDim(p, d)? This file proves the lower bound direction (from subgroup monotonicity) and axiomatizes the upper bound (the open conjecture), then derives specific cases: buDim(4, d) = buDim(2, d), buDim(6, d) = max(buDim(2,d), buDim(3,d)), and buDim(9, d) = buDim(3, d).

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: 1 axiom: buDim_le_formula (the open conjecture: buDim(n,d) ≤ max_{p|n} buDim(p,d)). Lower bound direction proved from buDim_mono in parent file. Specific cases n=4,6,9 proved. buDim function and known results axiomatized in parent file BorsukUlamOQ02OQ01.lean. The specific cases n=4,6,9 are discharged via `native_decide` (computing `Nat.primeFactors 4 = {2}`, `{2,3}`, `{3}`), so those presented theorems additionally depend on `Lean.ofReduceBool` (kernel-trusted compiler reduction). Counting this compiler-trust assumption alongside the buDim_le_formula axiom gives meta.axiomCount = 2; leanFile.axiomCount = 1 counts only the literal `axiom` declaration.

overview.historicalContext: The equivariant Borsuk-Ulam theorem for Z/n-actions asks: what is the minimum sphere dimension before Z/n-equivariant maps to d-dimensional spaces must vanish? For prime p, Yang (1954) gave the exact answer: buDim(p, 2n) = 2n-1. For composite n, the answer is controlled by the prime factorization, but the precise formula is open. The conjecture that buDim(n, d) = max_{p|n} buDim(p, d) — that composite groups add no extra topological constraint beyond their prime subgroups — is supported by Smith theory (for prime powers) and Yang-Borsuk lifting (for standard representations), but remains unproved in full generality. The Fadell-Husseini index theory (1988) provides the main tool for attacking this problem.
overview.problemStatement: For composite n ≥ 2, is buDim(n, d) = max_{p|n, p prime} buDim(p, d)?
overview.text: The BU dimension formula for composite cyclic groups: does the maximum over prime divisors exactly determine the equivariant dimension?
overview.proofStrategy: The lower bound buDimFormula(n,d) ≤ buDim(n,d) is proved: each prime p|n gives buDim(p,d) ≤ buDim(n,d) by restriction monotonicity (buDim_mono from parent file), so the supremum over primes is also ≤ buDim(n,d). The upper bound buDim(n,d) ≤ buDimFormula(n,d) is axiomatized as the open conjecture. Specific consequences for n=4,6,9 are derived using native_decide to compute Nat.primeFactors.
keyInsights: The lower bound (formula ≤ buDim) is immediate from restriction monotonicity: any Z/n-equivariant map restricts to a Z/p-equivariant map for p|n
The upper bound (buDim ≤ formula) is the substantive open direction: it requires showing composite group structure never exceeds prime subgroup structure
For prime powers p^k, Smith theory implies buDim(p^k, d) = buDim(p, d), confirming the formula. This gives buDim(4,d) = buDim(2,d) and buDim(9,d) = buDim(3,d)
For Z/6 = Z/2 × Z/3: both Z/2 and Z/3 give the same bound (2n-1 for even d), so the maximum over prime factors equals each individual prime factor bound
Nat.primeFactors is computable in Mathlib 4, so specific values (primeFactors 4 = {2}, primeFactors 6 = {2,3}, primeFactors 9 = {3}) can be verified by native_decide

The conjecture is the index-theoretic shadow of a detection-at-primes principle. The cohomology of a cyclic group splits p-locally as the cohomology of its Z/p^{a_p} factor (the cohomological Chinese Remainder Theorem: H*(BZ/n) ≅ ⊗_p H*(BZ/p^{a_p})), so the Fadell-Husseini index — which lives in that ring — ought to be controlled prime-by-prime. buDim(n,d) = max_{p|n} buDim(p,d) is exactly what this prime-local decomposition predicts, mirroring how group cohomology is detected on Sylow subgroups via the transfer
prerequisites: Yang-Borsuk theorem for prime cyclic groups

sections.title: Module Header and Problem Context
sections.summary: Documentation header stating the central open question: for composite n >= 2, is buDim(n,d) = max over prime divisors p of buDim(p,d)? File proves the lower bound (from monotonicity) and axiomatizes the upper bound. Imports Nat.Prime.Basic, Finset.Basic, Tactic, and the parent BorsukUlamOQ02OQ01.
sections.mathContext: Open conjecture: $\text{buDim}(n,d) = \max_{p | n,\, p\text{ prime}} \text{buDim}(p,d)$ for composite $n \geq 2$. Lower bound $\leq$ proved; upper bound $\geq$ is axiomatized.

sections.title: The Dimension Formula Definition
sections.summary: Defines buDimFormula(n,d) = Nat.primeFactors(n).sup (fun p => buDim p d), the maximum BU dimension over all prime divisors of n.
sections.mathContext: Uses Finset.sup on the prime factorization: the supremum over {buDim p d | p prime, p | n}. Empty for n=1 giving 0.

sections.title: Lower Bound (Proved)
sections.summary: Proves buDimFormula(n,d) ≤ buDim(n,d) via Finset.sup_le + Nat.mem_primeFactors + buDim_mono.
sections.mathContext: For each p ∈ primeFactors(n): buDim(p,d) ≤ buDim(n,d) by restriction. Finset.sup_le packages this into the formula bound.

sections.title: Upper Bound: Prime Case and the Open Conjecture
sections.summary: buDimFormula_prime (proved): for prime n the upper bound buDim(n,d) ≤ buDimFormula(n,d) is immediate. buDim_le_formula_composite (AXIOM): the composite case buDim(n,d) ≤ max_{p|n} buDim(p,d) is the open conjecture. buDim_le_formula dispatches n ≥ 2 into the proved prime case and the axiomatized composite case.
sections.mathContext: Equivalent to: the Fadell-Husseini index of a Z/n-space is bounded by the maximum FH index over prime subgroups.

sections.title: The Formula Theorem
sections.summary: buDim_eq_formula: for n ≥ 2, buDim(n,d) = buDimFormula(n,d), combining the proved lower bound with the (partly axiomatized) upper bound into the two-sided identity.
sections.mathContext: $\text{buDim}(n,d)=\max_{p\mid n}\text{buDim}(p,d)$ for $n\ge2$ — the conjectured formula, two-sided.

sections.title: Formula at Primes
sections.summary: buDimFormula_prime and buDim_prime_eq_formula: for a prime p the formula recovers buDim(p,d) directly (primeFactors p = {p}), so the conjecture holds trivially at primes — the base case of the reduction.

sections.title: Concrete Cases
sections.summary: Discharges small composite cases via native_decide on Nat.primeFactors: buDim(4,d)=buDim(2,d), buDim(6,d)=max(buDim(2,d),buDim(3,d)), buDim(9,d)=buDim(3,d). These evaluate primeFactors 4={2}, 6={2,3}, 9={3}, then apply the formula theorem — depending on Lean.ofReduceBool.
sections.mathContext: $\mathbb{Z}/4$ and $\mathbb{Z}/2$ share BU dimension; $\mathbb{Z}/9=\mathbb{Z}/3^2$ collapses to $\mathbb{Z}/3$; $\mathbb{Z}/6$ takes the max over its prime factors $2,3$.

sections.title: Prime Powers (General)
sections.summary: buDimFormula_prime_pow and buDim_prime_pow_eq: the formula collapses at any prime power p^k (k ≥ 1) to the single prime p, so prime powers do not increase the BU dimension — the general form of the n=4,9 concrete collapses.

sections.title: Specific BU Dimensions
sections.summary: Closed-form BU dimensions: buDim(4,n+1)=n (Z/4-equivariant odd maps S^n → R^{n+1} must vanish) and buDim(6,2n)=2n-1 for n ≥ 1 (both prime-factor bounds of 6 coincide at 2n-1).
sections.mathContext: $\text{buDim}(4,n+1)=n$ and $\text{buDim}(6,2n)=2n-1$ — explicit values from the formula.

conclusion.summary: Formalizes the BU dimension formula conjecture for composite n: buDim(n,d) = max_{p|n} buDim(p,d). Lower bound proved from subgroup monotonicity. Upper bound axiomatized. Specific cases n=4,6,9 derived with 0 sorries.
conclusion.implications: If the conjecture is true, the equivariant BU dimension of any cyclic group is completely determined by its prime factors — a remarkable reduction from composite group theory to prime group theory. This would mean the Fadell-Husseini ideal-valued index satisfies a prime factorization property analogous to the multiplicativity of cohomology.
openQuestions: Can the upper bound buDim(n,d) ≤ buDimFormula(n,d) be proved in Lean using the Fadell-Husseini index from the sister file BorsukUlamOQ02OQ01OQ04.lean?
Are there exotic G-representations where composite groups give strictly higher BU dimensions than any prime subgroup?
What is the relationship between buDim(p^k, d) and buDim(p, d) for all k, not just via the conjecture?

crossReferences.description: Extends the parent file's abstract BU dimension framework with the conjectured formula and its consequences
The Fadell-Husseini index theory provides the main theoretical tool for proving the open conjecture axiomatized here

The classical Borsuk-Ulam theorem is the Z/2 (antipodal) base case of this equivariant hierarchy: buDim with the prime p=2 recovers the statement that every f: Sⁿ → ℝⁿ has an antipodal coincidence. The composite-n formula generalizes it to arbitrary cyclic group actions

A kindred topological-obstruction theorem: Borsuk-Ulam classically implies the Brouwer fixed-point theorem, and both are instances of degree/index arguments showing certain continuous maps cannot avoid a forced coincidence or fixed point

Sperner's lemma is the combinatorial backbone of fixed-point and Borsuk-Ulam-type results; its n-dimensional form gives a constructive, discrete route to the same topological obstructions that the Fadell-Husseini index measures cohomologically here
